A group of crows is called a murder.

The provided text discusses quantum computing, specifically highlighting the use of qubits to revolutionize cryptography and drug discovery. This concept can be linked to existing knowledge in computer science and biology databases. In cryptography, the shift from classical bits to quantum qubits necessitates the development of post-quantum cryptography to secure data against quantum attacks. In pharmaceuticals, the ability of qubits to model complex molecular structures simultaneously allows for more accurate simulations of drug interactions, accelerating the discovery process for new medicines. These connections illustrate how quantum mechanics principles are applied to solve complex problems in information security and healthcare.
